title: Sounds English? It's Swedish. The Englund Gambit
desc: While England celebrates Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or, here's an opening that only sounds English.

title: 10 Opening Traps Every Beginner Must Know
desc: 10 opening traps every beginner must know, from Scholar's Mate to the Siberian Trap. For each trap you see the setup, the bait, how it punishes you, and the fix so you never fall for it. Every line checked with Stockfish

title: Free queen? Mate in 2! Légal's Mate
desc: Free queen? Mate in 2! Légal's Mate is almost 300 years old and still works: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 d6 3.Bc4 Bg4 4.Nc3 g6? 5.Nxe5! Bxd1?? 6.Bxf7+ Ke7 7.Nd5#.

title: Free rook? Don't take it! Giri vs Abdusattorov
desc: Anish Giri left his rook hanging… on purpose. European Club Cup 2026, Giri vs Abdusattorov: after 17...Bg4?! Giri ignored the threat with 18.Bb2!, Black grabbed the rook with 18...Bxd1?? and 19.Nf5! 20.Qg5! hit g7 and th

title: Take my queen! The Stafford Gambit trap
desc: Black gives away the queen… and wins. The Stafford Gambit trap: after 5.d3 Bc5 6.Bg5?? Nxe4! 7.Bxd8?? Bxf2+ 8.Ke2 Bg4# it's checkmate.

title: Don't take the bait! The Fishing Pole Trap
desc: The Fishing Pole Trap: Black leaves a knight on g4 as bait. Take it with hxg4?? and the h-file opens straight at your king, ending in mate on h1.

title: Fried Liver Attack: mate in 9 (and how to stop it)
desc: The Fried Liver Attack: after 4.Ng5 d5 5.exd5 Nxd5? 6.Nxf7! the black king is dragged out, and if it runs home, Bxe6 is mate. How to stop it: don't recapture on d5. Play 5...Na5! and hit the bishop.

title: Don’t fall for this Petrov trap
desc: I copied his move… and lost my queen. After 3...Nxe4? 4.Qe2! the knight is pinned: one wrong move and Nc6+ is a discovered check that wins the queen. The fix: play 3...d6 first, then take on e4.

title: Stop the Scholar’s Mate (and punish it)
desc: Your opponent brings the queen out early? Block with g6, defend f7 with Nf6, then hit the queen with Nd4. One wrong queen move and Nxc2+ wins the rook.

title: He moved his king on move 5… big mistake 👑
desc: My opponent moved his king by hand on move 5 and lost the right to castle. A knight fork, a won rook and a little trap later, it was checkmate in 12.

title: I fell for the oldest trick in chess 😩
desc: The Scholar’s Mate pattern: queen and bishop team up against f7, Black’s weakest square. I even saw the threat and blocked it… then one “active” queen move later, f7 was undefended again.
